activity: spending a surprise snow day at home
knowledge_domain: spending a surprise snow day at home
fact: Grown-ups shovel snow off paths so people can walk without slipping.
story:
Rehmat woke up and saw white. Snow was on the grass. Snow was on the car. Snow was on the path. "No school today," said Mama. "It is a snow day." Rehmat was hungry, so Mama made warm toast.

Then they heard a sound. Beep, beep. "The mail is coming," said Rehmat. But the path was deep in snow. The mail carrier might slip. Papa got the big shovel. Rehmat got her little red shovel. She pushed one pile, then two piles, then three piles of snow. It was slow work. She kept going.

The mail carrier walked up the clean path. No slipping. "Thank you," she said, and put a letter in the box. Rehmat looked at her mittens. The snow on them began to melt into little wet spots. "One shovel, one path, one letter," said Rehmat. Papa laughed and scooped her up.

activity: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
knowledge_domain: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
fact: Yesterday is the day before today.
story:
Charles sat at the dinner table. He saw a bowl of peas. He did not want peas.

"Can we have pasta?" he asked. "We had it tomorrow."

Dad smiled and put a hand on his shoulder. "We had pasta yesterday," said Dad. "Yesterday is the day before today. You ate it before this day."

Charles looked down. He wiggled his tiny toe inside his sock under the table. He thought hard. "So yesterday is done?" he asked. "It already went by?"

"Yes," said Dad. "It went by."

"And today is now?"

"Today is now," said Dad. "Later we can have pasta."

Charles picked up his spoon. He took one small bite of peas. "Then I will eat some now," he said. "Pasta comes later."

Mom brought warm bread from the kitchen. She tore a piece for Charles. He dipped it in the peas.

"Now peas," he said. "Later pasta."

Dad laughed. "That is right, Charles. Tomorrow we can have pasta too."

Charles grinned and took another bite.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
fact: Toys cannot really feel, but you can pretend they do.
story:
Raphael was at daycare. Mia was crying. She had dropped her doll on the floor. "Baby fell down," Mia said.

Raphael looked at the doll. It was on the mat. It did not move. It did not cry. Hmm, thought Raphael. Do dolls cry? He picked the doll up. He gave it a big hug. "There, there," he said softly. Mia stopped crying. She looked at the doll. "Is baby okay?" she asked.

"Baby is okay," said Raphael. "She wants a sock. A thick one, for her cold toes." Mia laughed. She found a tiny sock in the toy box. She put it on the doll's foot. "Baby says thank you," said Raphael, in a small baby voice. Mia hugged the doll too.

Then Mia fed the doll a pretend bottle. Raphael patted the doll's back. The doll made a pretend burp. Both children laughed out loud. Teacher Sam smiled and came to sit with them. "Can baby have one more sock?" he asked.

Raphael held up the doll's bare little foot. "Yes," he said. "This one is cold too."

activity: spending a surprise snow day at home
knowledge_domain: spending a surprise snow day at home
fact: A snowplow pushes snow off the road.
story:
David woke up. Snow was everywhere. No school today. "Snow day!" said Mom.

David looked out the window. The road was white. The road was all covered up. "How will we go sledding?" he asked.

Then David heard a big noise. A huge truck came down the street. It had a big blade in front. The blade pushed the snow off the road. David watched. The road turned black again. The snow piled up on the side.

"The truck cleaned the road!" said David.

"Yes," said Mom. "Get your boots."

At the sledding hill, David climbed up. He sat on his sled. "Be careful," said Mom. David went down, down, down. Snow flew up like little fish jumping in the sky.

"Again!" said David. He climbed up the hill one more time.

activity: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
knowledge_domain: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
fact: A game has rules that all the players follow.
story:
Elizabeth ran to the slide at the park. Her friend Mia was already there. So was a boy named Sam. "Let's take turns," said Mia. "We go one at a time."

Elizabeth went first. Then Mia went. Then it was Sam's turn. Sam slid down fast. Then he ran back to the ladder. "My turn again!" he said. "You changed the rules," said Mia. "The rule is we take turns. One, two, three." Sam grabbed the ladder and would not move.

Mia sat down on the grass. Elizabeth sat down too. Nobody was on the slide. Sam looked at his friends. They were not playing. Sam let go of the ladder. "Okay," he said. "I will wait my turn." He stood at the end of the line.

Elizabeth slid down. Mia slid down. Then Sam had his turn. He waited for his next turn all by himself. "Good waiting," said Mia. She shared her round ball with Sam. They rolled it back and forth on the grass. Elizabeth's mom sat on a bench nearby. She waved. Elizabeth waved back. "Same time tomorrow?" asked Sam. "Yes," said Elizabeth. "Same rules, too."

activity: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
knowledge_domain: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
fact: Shirts, socks and hats are all clothes.
story:
Emily sat in her car seat. She held her little bag of things. The car went bump, bump, down the road.

"I want my teddy," said Emily. She looked in her bag. She pulled out a sock. "That is not a teddy!" she said. She laughed. She pulled out a shirt. "Not a teddy either!" Then she found a hat. "Silly hat," she said, and she put it on the teddy. A sock, a shirt and a hat were all in the bag together. "Are you all clothes?" Emily asked the bag. She looked again. "Yes! Clothes, clothes, clothes." Then her hand found something soft at the bottom. It was the teddy! "There you are," she said, and she hugged him tight.

A little spider crawled up the window outside. Tap, tap. It looked like it wanted to knock and come in. "No, spider," said Emily. "This car is for teddies and clothes." Daddy laughed from the front seat. "Safe and sound," he said. Emily gave the teddy one more hug. Then the car went bump, bump, all the way home.

activity: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
knowledge_domain: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
fact: Families get a bed or sleeping spot ready for a guest who stays the night.
story:
Grandpa was coming to stay for a whole week. Bennett wanted Grandpa to sleep in his room. But there was no bed for Grandpa yet. That was a problem.

Bennett went with Mama to the market. They pushed a little cart. "I want a soft pillow," Bennett said. He touched one pillow. Too bumpy. He touched another. Too big. Then he found a small blue one. "This one is soft!" He put it in the cart. Next to it sat a fresh loaf of bread for Grandpa's breakfast.

At home, Mama set up the small guest bed. Bennett put the blue pillow at the top. He ran and got his blanket with turtles on it. He spread it flat. He tried to make it smooth. It looked cozy.

The doorbell rang. Grandpa came in with his bag. He saw the little bed. He saw the turtle blanket. He sat down and patted the pillow. "A bed all ready for me," said Grandpa. Bennett climbed up for a hug. Grandpa said, "Best pillow at the whole market."

activity: starting the first day of school
knowledge_domain: starting the first day of school
fact: A school day has a time for eating a snack or lunch.
story:
Ayla ran into the school cafeteria. It was her first day! She looked at one long table, two long tables, three long tables. So many chairs. So many kids.

Then her tummy made a sound. Grrrumble! Ayla was hungry. She wanted lunch right now. "Can I eat now?" she asked Miss Jo. Miss Jo shook her head and smiled. "Not yet. First we go to our room." Ayla did not know about school days yet.

So Ayla waited. She sang a song. She stacked blocks. She drew a cat, a dog, and a smelly sock, because that made her laugh. Then Miss Jo clapped her hands. "Snack time!" The whole class walked to the cafeteria. Ayla sat down and opened her little bag. One apple, two crackers, three berries. She bit the apple. Crunch! A surprise jumped out of her bag. It was her winter mitten, hiding all along!

"Snack time comes every day," said her new friend Ben. Ayla laughed and held up her mitten like a flag.

activity: making an art or craft project
knowledge_domain: making an art or craft project
fact: Wet paint smears if you touch it before it dries.
story:
Sarah sat at the big table. Mom gave her paper and paint. Sarah dipped her brush in the yellow cup. She painted a big round sun. She painted green grass too. The paint smelled like rain in a garden.

Sarah wanted to hold her picture up. She grabbed it with her hand. Her thumb pressed on the sun. The yellow paint smeared. The sun now had a yucky smudge on it. Sarah's lip went wobbly. "My sun is messy," she said.

Mom sat down next to her. "Let's look at it," Mom said. Mom touched the paper with one finger. "Still wet," she said. "Wet paint makes smudges." Mom got a new sheet of paper. "This time we can wait."

Sarah painted a new sun. It was big and round and yellow. She put her brush down. Then she put her hands under her legs. She sat very still. She watched the paint shine. It looked wet and shiny, like a puddle.

Sarah waited and waited. She ate some crackers while she waited. She glued a cotton ball cloud onto the paper. Then Mom touched the corner. "All dry now," Mom said. Sarah picked up her picture with two careful hands. The sun stayed round and bright. No smudge at all. "I did it!" Sarah said. Mom clapped, and Sarah held her sun up to the window.

activity: weather words such as sunny, rainy, windy and snowy and the clothes that go with them
knowledge_domain: weather words such as sunny, rainy, windy and snowy and the clothes that go with them
fact: On a windy day, you can see trees sway and leaves blow around.
story:
Billie stood at the bus stop with her mother. The sun was out. It was a sunny day. Billie wore her sun hat. "Where is the bus?" she asked. "It is coming soon," said her mother.

Then the wind came. The trees began to sway. Big sway, little sway, sway, sway, sway. Leaves blew all around the bus stop. One red leaf blew right past Billie's nose. "I will catch it!" she said. She ran after the leaf. The leaf blew left. Billie ran left. The leaf blew right. Billie ran right.

The leaf stopped by a thick bush. Billie grabbed it. "I caught you!" she said. She held the leaf up high. The wind blew again and her hat flew off. The hat rolled down the sidewalk. Billie chased her hat too. Her mother laughed and picked it up. "Wind, you are silly," said Billie.

Then rain began to fall. Plip, plip, plip. Her mother opened a big umbrella. "Where is the sun now?" asked Billie. "Hiding behind the clouds," said her mother. The bus came at last. Billie climbed on with her leaf and her hat. "Next time, I want snow," said Billie.

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
fact: The last place you remember having something is a good place to start looking.
story:
Maeve rides the city bus with Grandma. Maeve holds her little bunny. The bus bumps and bounces. Now Maeve looks down. Bunny is gone.

"Oh no," says Maeve. "Where is bunny?"

Grandma holds her hand. "Let's look," says Grandma. Maeve checks under the seat. No bunny. Maeve checks her bag. No bunny. She looks at the floor by the door. No bunny.

Maeve thinks hard. "I had bunny on my lap," she says. "I gave him a pretend crumb from my snack." Grandma smiles. "Then let's look right there," she says. Maeve lifts her sweater, which had slipped down in a big heap. There sits bunny, tucked straight under it. "I catch you!" Maeve says, and hugs him tight.

The bus stops. Grandma picks up the bags. Maeve sits back with bunny on her lap, both hands around him all the way home.

activity: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
knowledge_domain: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
fact: The word 'five' and the numeral 5 mean the same number.
story:
Ryan wore his gray sweater to daycare. Snow was falling outside the window. Miss Jo held up a big card. It had a 5 on it. Ryan did not know that sign.

The class sang the counting song. "One, two, three, four, five." Ryan looked at his hand. He counted his fingers. One, two, three, four, five. Then he looked at the card again. The 5 was the same as his five fingers.

Now the class went to play. Miss Jo said, "Find the door with five." Ryan saw doors with 2 and 3. He held up one hand. He counted all five fingers. Then he saw it. A door with a big 5.

"That one," said Ryan. He opened the door. Inside were five little trucks, waiting on the shelf.

activity: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
knowledge_domain: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
fact: Day and night are opposites.
story:
Lily was at school. It was time to sleep on her little mat. The room was dark. Lily closed her eyes. One, two, three, she counted sheep. Then she slept.

Lily woke up. She saw dark. She thought, "It is morning!" She sat up fast. "Time to play!" she began to shout. The teacher came over. "Shh," she said. "Look out the window." Lily looked. The sky was dark. The moon was up. It was still night, not day. Night and day were not the same. Lily lay back down. One, two, three, she counted sheep again.

Later the sun came up. The room turned light. Day was here now. Lily got up slow, not fast. She put on her shoes. One shoe, two shoes. On the table there was a letter for each child. Lily found her letter. It had a big L on it. Her friend Tom's letter had a small t.

At snack time, Lily touched a wet cup. "Slimy," she said, and wiped her hands. The teacher gave out warm bread. She poured cold milk. Lily took a big bite. Then a small sip. Outside the window, a bird flew fast. A snail went slow, slow, slow on a leaf. Lily watched the snail all the way to the edge. "Bye, snail," she said.

activity: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
knowledge_domain: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
fact: Wheels are round like circles, which lets them roll.
story:
Gabriel wanted to make a toy car. He found a small box in the toy basket. The box had four sides, like a square. "Good car body," said Papa.

Now Gabriel needed wheels. He took some cardboard. Papa helped him cut four little squares. Gabriel taped them on. Square wheels, one, two, three, four. He pushed the car on the floor. The car went thump, thump, thump. It did not roll. "Silly car!" said Gabriel. He laughed his loud laugh.

Papa held the scissors. He cut the squares into circles. Round wheels, one, two, three, four. Gabriel pushed the car again. It rolled fast, fast, fast. It rolled under the chair. Gabriel got down on his arm and tummy to catch it. "My car rolls!" he said. "Go, circle wheels, go!"

activity: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
knowledge_domain: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
fact: The counting words always go in the same order: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
story:
Madison went to the library with her brother Sam. Sam was little. He wanted to count the toy ducks. He touched each duck. "One, two, four," said Sam.

Madison tilted her head. Was that right? She sang the counting song in her head. "One, two, three, four," she sang out loud. Sam pushed a duck toward her. "Say it with me," said Madison. "One, two, three, four." Sam tried. "One, two, three, four!" Now four ducks had names.

Then Sam got stuck again. He counted the library chairs. "One, two, three, four, five, seven," he said. Madison thought hard. What came after five? She sang the song again, slower. "Five, six." Sam tapped the next chair. "Six!" he said. Then he kept going. "Seven, eight, nine, ten."

After the library, they walked to the park. Sam counted the swings. The words came out in the right order, all the way to three. Madison slid down the slippery slide and laughed. "How high can you count tomorrow?" she asked Sam. Sam held up his hands and grinned. "Ten!"

activity: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
knowledge_domain: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
fact: We say "thank you" when someone gives us something or helps us.
story:
Charlotte was painting at the big table. Mama sat next to her. Charlotte painted a fat yellow bee with black stripes.

The doorbell rang. Grandma came in with a small red bag. Inside was a new blue hat for Charlotte. Charlotte put it on right away. She ran to the mirror. The hat looked just right.

Grandma sat down and waited. She looked at the door. Then she looked at the floor. Charlotte stopped. She took off the hat. She ran back to Grandma. "Thank you, Grandma!" she said. Grandma smiled a big smile. She gave Charlotte a hug.

Charlotte went back to her paint. She painted Grandma a bee hat too. Grandma laughed. "My turn to say thank you," she said.

activity: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
knowledge_domain: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
fact: Hold a grown-up's hand when you cross the street.
story:
Sarah was in the bathroom. She wanted to wash her hands all by herself. Dad turned the tap for her. "This side is cold," Dad said. "The red side makes hot water. I will turn it for you." Sarah felt the cold water on her hands. It felt nice and fresh. She rubbed the soap and made white bubbles. Dad waited by the door.

After her bath, Sarah put on her socks. Then she heard something. "Do you hear that?" she asked. Dad said, "Yes! The ice cream truck." Sarah wanted ice cream. The truck was across the street. She looked out the window. Cars went by, fast and slow.

"Can we go?" Sarah asked. "Yes," said Dad. "But first, what do we need?" Sarah looked at the street. Then she looked at her hand. She held it up to Dad. Dad took her hand in his big old hand. They stopped at the curb. They looked left. They looked right. The cars stopped. Then they walked across together.

Sarah got a pink ice cream. She licked it and smiled at Dad. "We held hands," she said. Dad gave her a big hug right there on the park grass.

activity: common daily routines such as eating, sleeping, bathing and getting dressed
knowledge_domain: common daily routines such as eating, sleeping, bathing and getting dressed
fact: A grown-up checks the bath water to make sure it is not too hot before you get in.
story:
Emilia ate her toast in the kitchen. Crumbs fell on the floor. "I can sweep them," she said. She got the little brush and swept. The crumbs went into the dustpan.

Then Mama said, "Bath time." Emilia ran to the tub. She wanted to jump right in. But she stopped. Mama put her hand in the water first. "Too hot," said Mama. She added some cool water. She put her hand in again. "Now it is just right."

Emilia put one toe in. The water felt warm and nice. She climbed in with Mama's help. She splashed and played with the yellow duck.

After the bath, Mama helped her get dressed in soft pajamas. Emilia yawned. She hugged her bear. Soon her eyes closed and she fell fast asleep while Mama sang a quiet song. The phone rang, but Mama let it ring and kept singing softly.

activity: getting a first haircut at a salon
knowledge_domain: getting a first haircut at a salon
fact: Hair grows back after it is cut.
story:
Elijah sat in the big waiting room. He was waiting for his first haircut. He did not want one. "My hair will fall off," he said. "It will be gone forever."

Mom held his hand. A man with long dark hair walked by. "Look," Mom said. "His hair grew long."

Elijah peeked at the barber's chair. The scissors made a snip, snip sound. A little girl sat very tall in the seat. Clippings fell on the floor. Then she jumped down and smiled. "It works," she said. "The chair goes up and down!"

Elijah sat very still in the chair. The barber snipped and snipped. Hair fell like little dark pieces of string. Elijah watched them drop.

At home, Elijah looked in the mirror. His hair was short. He touched his head. It felt soft. "Grow back fast, hair," he whispered.

Mom laughed. "You will see it grow." Elijah smiled and patted his head two times.

activity: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
knowledge_domain: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
fact: Ten is written with two digits, a 1 and then a 0.
story:
Zoey wanted to make a special picture for Grandma. She drew one sun. She drew two clouds. She drew three red apples, and she wanted to eat every one. She counted the apples out loud. "One, two, three." Then she drew more. Four flowers, five birds, six shoes, seven cups, eight hats, nine cats. She wrote the numbers on her picture, too. Each number had one shape.

Now Zoey wanted to draw ten cats. She sang her counting song. "Eight, nine, ten." Ten! She tried to write ten. She made one shape. It did not look right. She looked at her brother's book. There it was. Ten used two shapes, a 1 and then a 0. Zoey wrote them. A 1 and then a 0. She looked and looked. Ten! She drew one more cat.

"Ten cats for Grandma," said Zoey.

activity: starting the first day of school
knowledge_domain: starting the first day of school
fact: On the school bus, children stay sitting in their seats.
story:
Grace stood in the school hallway. It was her first day. Her tummy felt like butterflies.

Grace had ridden the school bus. She had seen a big cat on the street. She wanted to wave at it. She stood up on her seat. The driver said, "Please sit down." So Grace sat down fast. The bus bumped and wiggled. Grace held on tight. Then she waved from her seat instead. The cat did not wave back. Silly cat!

In the hallway, Grace saw a boy. He was crying big tears. Grace wanted to help. She waved at him. He did not wave back. So Grace made a funny face. The boy froze. Then he giggled. He made a funny face back. Grace laughed too.

Then Grace's teacher called, "Time for class!" Grace took the boy's hand. They walked together. Grace let him go through the door first. "You can be last," the boy said. "No," said Grace. "You go first." And they both laughed all the way in.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
fact: Holding your nose closed makes food taste less strong.
story:
Milan went to the park with his dad. Milan saw a bird with his eyes. He heard it sing with his ears. He smelled flowers with his nose. Then they sat on the grass. Dad opened the picnic bag.

"Strawberries!" said Milan. He touched one with his fingers. It felt bumpy and cold. He took a big bite. "Mmm, so sweet!"

Then Milan pinched his nose closed. He took another bite. The strawberry tasted plain, like nothing much. He let go of his nose. He took one more bite. The sweet taste came back! "Dad, the taste went away when I held my nose!"

Dad laughed. "Try the apple too," he said. Milan held his nose and bit the apple. Plain again! Then he let go. Crunch, sweet, yum.

An elephant statue stood by the swings. "That elephant is lucky," said Milan. "It has a big nose." He ran to touch the cool gray stone. "Can the elephant smell strawberries?" he asked. Dad smiled and handed him one more.

activity: learning to play a musical instrument
knowledge_domain: learning to play a musical instrument
fact: After playing for an audience, musicians often bow when people clap.
story:
Maria went to Miss Kim's music room. She was learning to play the drum. First she would build a tall tower of sounds. Boom, boom, boom went her hands.

"Play it for me," said Miss Kim. "I am your audience today." Maria played her drum. Boom, boom, boom. The room felt hot from all her jumping. She played loud like a lion, then soft like a little cat. Miss Kim clapped and clapped. "Clap, clap, clap!" Maria stopped. She looked at Miss Kim's hands. They clapped more.

Maria remembered what she saw at the big concert. The man played his violin. Then he bent down low. Maria bent down low too. She bowed. Miss Kim clapped even louder now. "Again!" said Maria. She stood up. She played boom, boom, boom. Miss Kim clapped. Maria bowed down low, and her hair swung near her knees. "Yay!" said Miss Kim, and she clapped and clapped.

activity: spending a surprise snow day at home
knowledge_domain: spending a surprise snow day at home
fact: People wear hats, mittens, boots and warm coats to play in the snow.
story:
Abigail looked out the window. The park was white with snow. "Snow day!" said Mama. Abigail put on her warm coat. She put on her boots and her hat. Her mittens were still on the shelf.

Abigail ran to the park. She patted the snow. It was soft and cold. She made a big snowball with wide, red hands. Then her fingers began to hurt. They felt like ice. "Ow," said Abigail. She ran back home.

"My hands are cold," she said. Mama helped her put on her mittens. Then Abigail clapped her mittens together. Back at the park, she made a snow frog. It had round snow eyes. Her fingers stayed warm and cozy. "Hop, hop, little frog," said Abigail.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
fact: It is hard to see in the dark, so we turn on a light.
story:
Ivy went to the doctor with her teddy. The nurse said, "Time to check your ears." Ivy put teddy on a chair.

The doctor looked in Ivy's ears. "You hear with these," he said. Ivy heard a little beep. Then she saw a picture of a duck on the wall. She touched the cold stethoscope. She smelled soap on the doctor's hands. At the end, the nurse gave her a sweet sticker. Ivy stuck out her tongue. "I can taste the grape!" she said.

Then Ivy looked for teddy. Teddy was gone! The coat room door was open. The room was dark. Ivy could not see teddy anywhere. She felt sad and a bit grumpy. "I will look again," she said. She went slow. She patted the soft coats. No teddy. The nurse came in. "Let me help," she said. She turned on the light. Now the room was bright. There was teddy, under a red hat! Ivy held him tight. "The light helped me see," said Ivy. The nurse smiled and said, "Teddy and you make a good team."

activity: watching a big game with family and friends
knowledge_domain: watching a big game with family and friends
fact: When both teams have the same score, it is called a tie.
story:
Kayden ran to the big green field. The sun was warm on his face. Today the weather was good for a game. Mom held his hand. Dad carried a red blanket.

"Kick the ball!" Kayden shouted. The players ran fast. One team kicked. One team blocked. The crowd clapped and stomped. Kayden stomped his little feet too.

Then the whistle blew. The game was over. Everyone looked at the big board. Kayden pointed up. "Who won, Mom?"

Mom looked at the numbers. Both teams had two points. "The score is a tie," she said. Kayden frowned. He wanted a winner. He stamped his shoe on the grass.

Then both teams got a big shiny cup. They held it up together. The crowd cheered loud. Kayden clapped and clapped.

"Both teams win?" he asked.

"Both teams tie," said Dad, laughing.

Kayden spun in a circle. He did not dream of one winner anymore. He waved at the players. "Good game!" he called. The players waved back at him.

activity: cooking or baking a meal for the family
knowledge_domain: cooking or baking a meal for the family
fact: Cooks rinse dirt off vegetables like carrots and potatoes before cooking them.
story:
Isaac wanted to cook soup for his family. He ran to the backyard garden with his red bucket. He pulled up two fat carrots. Pop! One came out fast. The carrots were covered in dirt.

Isaac held up a carrot. "Yuck," he said. "Can we eat dirty carrots?"

Mom looked at the carrot. "Let's find out," she said.

At the sink, Isaac turned on the cold water. He scrubbed the carrots with his hands. The dirt washed away. The water turned brown. The carrots turned bright orange.

"Look, Mom! The dirt went down the drain!" Isaac said. "The carrots are clean now!"

Mom chopped the carrots with her big knife. Isaac watched from his stool. Mom boiled the soup on the hot stove. Soon the soup was ready.

Dad and Grandma came to the table. Everyone took a big slurp.

"Who made this soup?" Grandma asked.

"Me!" said Isaac. "I washed the carrots all by myself!"

Grandma held up her spoon. "More soup, please!"

activity: getting a first library card and borrowing a book
knowledge_domain: getting a first library card and borrowing a book
fact: Library books have a label on the spine that shows where the book belongs on the shelf.
story:
Luke ran into the storytime room. Today he would get his first library card! The librarian smiled. "Pick any book you like," she said. Luke found a book about a round pumpkin. Inside was a tiny black seed. He loved it.

A girl named Mia put her book back on the shelf. But it did not fit. The books next to it were big. Hers was small. Luke watched the librarian slide it out. She tapped the white label on the book's spine. Then she found the right spot. The book slid in just right.

Luke looked at his pumpkin book. It had a white label too! He matched it to the shelf. The book fit like a puzzle piece.

"You get to wear this on your backpack," said the librarian. She clipped on his new card. Luke held his book up high. "Let's go home and read about the seed!"

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
fact: Players drink water during breaks, especially on hot days.
story:
Violet was on the swim team. Her little team was called the Blue Fish. Today was a big, hot day at the pool.

Violet jumped in the water. She kicked her legs. She splashed to the other side. The coach blew the whistle. "Break time!" he called.

All the Blue Fish climbed out. They sat on the warm bench. Every player grabbed a water bottle. Everyone drank and drank. Violet looked in her bag. She looked again. Her water bottle was at home!

Violet began to wonder what to do. Then Coach Ben came over. He held out a little blue cup. "Here you go," he said. "Players drink water during breaks, especially on hot days."

Violet drank the cool water. It felt good in her throat. Her tummy felt happy too.

Then the whistle blew again. "Back in the pool!" said Coach Ben. Violet jumped up. She splashed into the water. She kicked her legs fast.

"Go, Violet!" her friend Mia called.

Violet swam and swam. The cool water washed over her arms. She reached the wall first. "I did it!" she said with a big smile.

Coach Ben laughed. "That was fast," he said. "Same time tomorrow?"

"Yes!" said Violet. "And I will bring my water bottle."

activity: getting a first library card and borrowing a book
knowledge_domain: getting a first library card and borrowing a book
fact: At storytime, a librarian reads books aloud to a group of children.
story:
Everly went to the big library with her dad. She wanted her very own library card. The lady at the desk said, "First, tell me your name." Everly said, "Everly! Like ever so much!" The lady laughed and made the card.

Then Everly heard a loud voice in the next room. "What is that?" she asked. Dad said, "Let's go see." A librarian sat in a circle of chairs. She opened a book about a cow who blew a trumpet. All the children laughed.

Everly hid behind dad's legs. Then the librarian turned a page. The cow blew the trumpet even louder. "MOO!" said the librarian. Everly giggled and sat right down.

After storytime, she picked the cow book. "My card," she said, and held it out. The lady beeped the book. Everly hugged it all the way home.

activity: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
knowledge_domain: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
fact: A balloon blown up with air from a person's breath does not float up to the ceiling.
story:
Mackenzie turned four today. Her party was at the bowling alley. She wore shiny red shoes with wheels on the bottom. Her dad helped her put them on. "These are my party shoes," she said.

The whole family came. Grandma came. Her friend Lily came too. There were bowling shoes to borrow. Mackenzie picked blue ones. "Blue like my birthday cake," she said.

Dad blew up a big yellow balloon. He gave it to Mackenzie to hold. She held it tight. Lily had a balloon too. It was pink. Lily let go of her balloon. It did not fly up. It went down, down, down to the floor. Mackenzie watched it land.

"Let me try," said Mackenzie. She let go of her balloon. It went down, down, down too. It landed right by her blue shoe. "Again!" she said. She picked it up and let go again. Down it went, right onto Lily's pink balloon.

Then came a small surprise. The yellow balloon landed on the cake table. It touched a bowl of salty pretzels. "My balloon wants a snack," said Mackenzie. Grandma laughed and laughed. Lily picked up both balloons. "Let's do it together," she said. They let go at the same time. Down, down, down, side by side. "Happy birthday to me," said Mackenzie, and she hugged the yellow balloon tight.

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
fact: Teams warm up by running or stretching before a game.
story:
Zayn ran onto the baseball diamond. "Play ball!" he shouted. He wanted to swing his bat right away.

Coach Maya blew her whistle. "First we warm up," she said. "Teams warm up by running or stretching before a game."

Zayn made a silly face. "Do bats warm up too?" he asked.

"Maybe they do," said Coach Maya. "Take yours for a little run."

Zayn ran around the bases. He held his bat up high. Then he stretched his arms way down deep, like a tall tree bending in the wind. His friend Ana copied him. "I'm a floppy noodle!" she said. Zayn laughed so hard he fell in the grass.

The game began. Zayn took a big swing. Crack! The ball flew far. "My legs feel fast!" he called to Ana.

"Told you," Ana said, and stuck out her tongue. Zayn chased her past first base.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
fact: An illustrator is a person who draws or paints the pictures for a book.
story:
Emily wanted her bunny book at bedtime. She could not find it in the pile. She looked under her bed. She looked in her toy box. "Not there," she said. Daddy helped her look. He found the book under a chair. "Here it is," he said.

Emily sat on the bed with Daddy. She opened the book from the front. The first page had words on it. "Read the words," she said. Daddy read them out loud. "This book was painted by Mr. Lee," he read. Emily touched the curly letters in his name. "Mr. Lee made my bunnies?" she asked. "Yes," said Daddy. "He is the person who paints the pictures for books."

Emily turned the pages one by one. She found a bunny with curly fur. "Mr. Lee painted this one too," she said. She smelled the pages. The air smelled like paper. Daddy read the whole book, front to back. On the last page was a small bunny sleeping. Emily smiled and whispered, "Goodnight, Mr. Lee."

activity: spending a surprise snow day at home
knowledge_domain: spending a surprise snow day at home
fact: Lying in the snow and sweeping your arms and legs makes a snow angel.
story:
Beatrice woke up and saw white. Snow! No school today. Mama said, "Snow day!" Beatrice put on her boots and her red hat.

They went to the sledding hill. Beatrice slid down, down, down. Then she fell off in the soft snow. She lay there and swept her arms. She swept her legs. She stood up and looked. There was an angel in the snow! But oh no. Her boot made a big smudge on it.

"Wait," said Beatrice. She found a different spot. She lay down carefully. She swept her arms. She swept her legs. Then she rolled to the side and stood up far away. The angel was perfect! "Two angels," she laughed. "One is sleepy."

On the way home, they saw a bird hopping in the snow. "He wants us to feed him," said Mama. They sprinkled seeds on a stump. The bird pecked one up fast. Beatrice waved. "Bye, bird! Make a snow angel too!"

activity: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
knowledge_domain: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
fact: A library puts its books on shelves in groups so people can find them.
story:
Rowan was in the backyard with his dad. He wanted his animal book. It had a bear on the cover. But the book was not in his toy box.

"Where is my bear book?" Rowan asked. Dad said, "Let's look inside." Rowan was worried. What if the book was lost?

Dad said, "We can go to the library. They have lots of books." Rowan put on his shoes. Dad got a cold frozen popsicle from the freezer for later.

At the library, a librarian took Rowan's hand. She walked to a big shelf. All the books on that shelf were about animals. Rowan saw a bird book, a dog book, and a fish book. And there was a bear book! The animal books sat together in one spot.

Rowan held the bear book tight. At home, he sat in the backyard. He made a stack of books by his chair. The animal books went in one stack. The truck books went in another stack. Dad brought the frozen popsicle and cut it in half.

Rowan licked his popsicle. He turned a page. The bear on the cover smiled at him.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
fact: When you close your eyes, you cannot see the things around you.
story:
Everly sat in a big chair at the doctor's office. She did not like shots. So she covered her eyes with her hands. "Now the doctor cannot see me," she thought. The nurse said, "Hello, Everly!" The doctor could still see her! Her hands hid only her own eyes.

The nurse held up a chart. "Can you read this line for me?" Everly looked with her eyes. She said the letters out loud. Then the nurse rang a little bell. Everly heard it with her ears. Ding, ding! "Where is it?" asked the nurse. Everly pointed. She had heard it just right.

The doctor gave her a round sticker. Everly touched it with her fingers. It was smooth. The room smelled like soap. Everly sniffed with her nose. "I smell it!" she said. At the end, the nurse gave her a cookie. Everly tasted it with her tongue. Yum. It was sweet.

Everly was not angry anymore. On the way out, she covered her eyes again. Then she peeked. The door was still there. The chairs were still there. "When I close my eyes, I can't see them," she said. She opened her eyes wide and waved. "Bye, doctor! Bye, bell!"

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
fact: Things can end up inside other things, like a toy tucked in a bag or coat pocket.
story:
Livia could not find her spotted bunny. She looked under the table. She looked behind the blocks. "Where can bunnies hide?" she asked. Miss Jo smiled. "Let us look some more," she said.

Livia looked in the toy box. No bunny. Then she saw her coat on the hook. The coat had a big pocket. Things could end up inside other things. She put her hand in the pocket. Something soft was in there. Out came the spotted bunny! "You were in my pocket all along," Livia said. She hugged bunny tight.

Then the pocket wiggled again. Livia pulled out a toy car too. It was Tim's little red car, lost last week. "I can speak to Tim at snack time," Livia said. She put bunny on her lap and drove the little car round and round.

activity: learning to play a musical instrument
knowledge_domain: learning to play a musical instrument
fact: Practicing a little every day helps you get better at playing.
story:
Anna went to the band room after her cookie snack. She picked up a little drum. Her teacher, Mr. Pip, showed her a song.

Anna hit the drum. Bong, bong, boom. She made a mistake. "Too hard!" said Anna. "I am afraid I will never get it."

"Try again tomorrow," said Mr. Pip. "And the next day too."

So Anna came back. She played a little bit. Then she played a little more. Each day she came back after snack time.

On Friday, Anna sat at the drum. Bong, bong, boom, bing! She played the whole song. No mistakes!

"Mr. Pip, listen!" she said.

He clapped his hands. "Now that is a song!"

Anna played it again, even louder.

activity: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
knowledge_domain: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
fact: If a cake has one candle for each year, a child turning five gets five candles.
story:
Jayden was at the park. It was his birthday party. Mom put a big cake on the table. The wind blew the napkins. Dad held them down. Everyone sang the birthday song. It was the same song as last year.

Jayden looked at his cake. He counted the candles. "One, two, three, four." Then he counted again. "One, two, three, four."

"How many candles should I have?" he asked Mom.

"Count how old you are," said Mom.

Jayden counted on his fingers. "I am one, two, three, four, five!"

"One candle for each year," said Mom. She took a small candle from her pocket. It was a red one. She pushed it into the cake.

"A red candle!" said Jayden. "That is my surprise!"

Dad lit the candles with a match. Jayden stood back, way back. The flames flickered in the wind. Everyone clapped.

"Make a wish," said Mom.

Jayden closed his eyes. The sun came out for a warm little spell. He blew out the candles, one, two, three, four, five.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
fact: An ice cube feels cold when you touch it.
story:
Peyton ran to the park with Dad. "Look, a juice stand!" she said. Dad bought her a cold juice with ice cubes in it.

Peyton poked an ice cube with her finger. "Ooh! Cold, cold, cold!" she cried. She pulled her hand back fast. Then she picked up the ice cube with her whole hand. It was so cold! She dropped it into her cup. Plink! It splashed. "It went in the water!" said Peyton.

Then she heard a loud sound. Honk, honk! A big black bird was by the fence. Peyton saw it flap its wings. She smelled popcorn. "I smell popcorn!" she said. Dad bought a bag. Peyton touched a bumpy kernel. It felt warm. She tasted one. "Yummy!" she said. Dad smiled. "Your hands are busy today!" Peyton held up her cold juice. "My hands, my eyes, my nose, my mouth!" she said. Then she took another big sip.
